summary:
Pernambuco recorded 7 killings of trans and travesti people in 2025, the second-highest raw count of any Brazilian state in the ANTRA dossier released on 26 January 2026, behind only Ceará and Minas Gerais at 8 each, against a national total of 80. In a state of some 9.1 million people this equals roughly 0.08 per 100,000 residents. Valor Internacional reported the same state-level counts on 27 January 2026, and Diario de Pernambuco carried the state ranking on the same date. The ranking is by raw count only; the sources provide no per-capita comparison between states.

The annual figure has fallen from 13 in 2022 to 9 in 2023, 8 in 2024 and 7 in 2025, so 2025 is the lowest count since 2022 while remaining among the highest in the country. Over six years Pernambuco recorded 83 violent deaths of trans people, the sixth-highest raw count in the national ranking for that period; the dossier counts 349 such killings across the Northeast from 2017 to 2025.

Killings are concentrated outside the Recife capital region. On 2 October 2025 a trans woman was shot dead inside her home in Belo Jardim, in the Agreste interior; the Civil Police opened an inquiry to identify the author and motive, and no arrests were reported at publication. On 7 July 2021 Fabiana da Silva Lucas, a 30-year-old Black trans woman, was found dead along highway PE-160 in Santa Cruz do Capibaribe, killed by several knife strikes, the state's third recorded killing of a trans or travesti person that month; police told press that a 22-year-old suspect known as 'Gaúcho' was lynched by locals at the scene.

Pernambuco operates its own anti-violence machinery. Law No. 18,634, signed by the president of the Legislative Assembly of Pernambuco on 13 July 2024 and instituted on 4 July 2024, establishes the State Policy for Combating Violence against LGBTQIA+ People, covering discrimination and violence based on gender identity, sexual orientation and sex characteristics. It recognises such violence as structural and incompatible with democratic rule, requires attention to intersecting race, territory, class, gender, age, religion and disability vulnerabilities, and mandates violence-data monitoring with a compiled methodology, protection and reception services, an emergency-support network for civil-society services, mapping and training of reception facilities, and data collection with research bodies.

In June 2026 state deputy João Paulo (PT) presented Bill No. 4.092/2026 to create a State Policy for Integral Health Promotion of the LGBTQIAPN+ population within the Unified Health System. The bill would reinforce the right to a social name in registrations and care, address travestis and transexuais who delay or avoid care for fear of mistreatment, direct health services to combat LGBTphobia and institutional discrimination, require continuous training of public health professionals, and mandate production and publication of LGBT health indicators.

The judiciary of Pernambuco has recognised gender identity directly. In 2023, following a 2022 lawsuit by the Public Defender's Office of Pernambuco, the Court of Justice of Pernambuco authorised Tarlazza Messina to change documents to reflect their gender identity, the first non-binary legal recognition in the state, registering gender as 'não binárie' on the birth certificate.

Municipal hostility has been checked. On 13 December 2017 Garanhuns enacted Municipal Law No. 4432/2017 banning discussion of gender theory in municipal schools, passed 11-to-1 despite a state prosecution recommendation to reject it. On 15 October 2025 the Supreme Federal Court struck the law down, lifting the ban on gender-related instruction in the city's schools.

Prison placement for trans detainees in Pernambuco stands under the national framework of National Council of Justice Resolution 348 of 13 October 2020, as amended by Resolution 366 of 2021: placement is decided by a judge after consulting the person, who must be told about male, female and LGBTI-specific units and whose declared preference is recorded, with LGBTI-specific spaces barred from use as disciplinary isolation. No Pernambuco-specific placement rule, special unit or documented case was identified in the sources; the state's prison administration (Secretaria de Administração Penitenciária e Ressocialização de Pernambuco) issues no trans-specific guidance in the material reviewed. Conjugal visitation for same-sex partners has been available in all Brazilian jails since February 2015 under the National Criminal and Penitentiary Council.
tangentialFactors:
The 2025 count of 7 is a raw figure; the sources give no per-capita comparison between Pernambuco and the states ranked above or below it, and Pernambuco's population of some 9.1 million makes it one of Brazil's larger states. A high raw count therefore does not by itself establish a higher per-capita rate than smaller states.

The national framework applies in Pernambuco alongside the state layer: legal gender recognition without surgery or judicial authorisation (STF, ADI 4275, 1 March 2018), transphobia treated as equivalent to racism since the Supreme Federal Court's 24 May 2019 vote of 6 of 11 justices, and nationwide prohibition of discrimination on gender-identity grounds since 2019.

Interior municipalities carry disproportionate risk relative to the capital. Both the October 2025 Belo Jardim killing and the July 2021 Santa Cruz do Capibaribe killing occurred in the Agreste, consistent with the dossier finding that most such killings in the state take place outside Recife.

The ANTRA methodology counts all media-reported killings of trans people irrespective of documented motive, and international comparisons are distorted by differences in documentation capacity; the 2025 figures should be read as reported counts rather than verified motive-specific tallies.
localsOnly:
Residents of Pernambuco are covered by Law No. 18,634 of 13 July 2024, the State Policy for Combating Violence against LGBTQIA+ People, which obliges the state executive to regulate and implement protection, reception and data-monitoring services statewide, prioritising victims of identity-based violence, those facing rupture of family or community ties, and those with compounded vulnerabilities.

Residents may seek gender-marker and name rectification through the civil registry under ADI 4275 without surgery or judicial authorisation; the Court of Justice of Pernambuco applied this in 2023 to recognise non-binary gender for the first time in the state, following a suit by the state Public Defender's Office.

Bill No. 4.092/2026, tabled in June 2026, would entrench social-name use and anti-discrimination duties inside Pernambuco's public health network; until enacted, SUS users in the state rely on existing national social-name rules and the bill's provisions are not binding.

Trans detainees held in Pernambuco's prison system are placed under national Council of Justice rules requiring a judge's reasoned decision after consultation, with recorded preference, transfer rights where violence or serious threat exists, and a prohibition on using LGBTI-specific units as disciplinary isolation. The state prison administration has issued no separate trans-placement instrument in the material reviewed.
outOfScopeNotes:
Whether Pernambuco's prison administration has issued internal guidance implementing Resolution 348/366, and whether the state operates dedicated LGBTI wings, is unresolved: the sources contain no state-level placement rule, unit designation or documented case.

The motive in the October 2025 Belo Jardim killing is unresolved; the Civil Police inquiry was open and no arrests were reported at publication, so the case is counted in the ANTRA tally but not established as an identity-motivated killing.

Bill No. 4.092/2026 had not been enacted at the time of the source material; its passage date and final content are not sourced.

The relationship between the state's raw-count ranking and per-capita risk is unresolved: the sources provide Pernambuco's population but no per-capita rates for the other states, so the second-place ranking cannot be read as a per-capita finding.
